nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry for Co redox dynamics in alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements conducted at different scan rates showcase the Co redox dynamics at different interfaces. The two pairs of redox peaks (anodic and cathodic) appearing from low to high applied potential are assigned to CoII/III (Vpa1 and Vpc1) and CoIII/IV (Vpa2 and Vpc2) transitions. Charge transferred during these two redox processes is reflected in the integrated CV area, which is approximately ×1.5 greater in the alkaline electrolyte than in the acidic and neutral electrolytes.

nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry for Co redox dynamics in neutral electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The separation between the Vpa2 and Vpc2 of CoIII/IV redox is the largest in a neutral electrolyte, indicating that CoIII/IV redox is electrochemically less reversible due to the slow interfacial electron transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nano-sized CoOx is composed primarily of spinel Co3O4 with a minor rocksalt CoO component.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nano-sized CoOx is composed primarily of spinel Co3O4 with a minor rocksalt CoO component (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ hard X-ray absorption spectroscopy characterization of nano CoOx shows bulk averaged Co oxidation state of around 2.52+, close to 2.67+ for the Co3O4 reference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ hXAS and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (sXAS) characterizations were performed to compare the bulk and surface oxidation states of nano CoOx catalyst to those of commercial Co3O4 and CoO references. The bulk averaged Co oxidation state of nano CoOx is around 2.52+, close to 2.67+ for the Co3O4 reference (Supplementary Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine-structure spectrum of nano-sized CoOx shows three representative scattering contributions of the spinel structure, with a Co–O distance of ~1.91 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine-structure (EXAFS) spectrum of nano-sized CoOx shows three representative scattering contributions of the spinel structure, with a Co–O of ~1.91 Å (Supplementary Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface-sensitive Co L3 spectra show coexistence of CoIII species and CoII species. Branching ratios of Co L3 and Co L2 edges calculated to be 0.58, indicating Co is in low-spin state. O K-edge spectra dominated by low-spin CoIII features.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface-sensitive Co L3 spectra show the coexistence of CoIII species and CoII species (Supplementary Fig. 4). The existence of low-spin CoIII is essential to ensure good OER performance in acidic environments. Accordingly, the branching ratios of Co L3 and Co L2 L2 edges were calculated to be 0.58 (Supplementary Table 2), suggesting that Co is in the low-spin state. The O K-edge spectra of nano-sized CoOx is dominated by the low-spin CoIII features in the region related to the Co 3d band.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry measurements at different scan rates showcase Co redox dynamics at different interfaces. Two pairs of redox peaks are assigned to CoII/III and CoIII/IV transitions. Charge transferred during these two redox processes is approximately 1.5 times greater in the alkaline electrolyte than in the acidic and neutral electrolytes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements conducted at different scan rates showcase the Co redox dynamics at different interfaces (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). The two pairs of redox peaks (anodic and cathodic) appearing from low to high applied potential are assigned to CoII/III (Vpa1 and Vpc1) and CoIII/IV (Vpa2 and Vpc2) transitions. Charge transferred during these two redox processes is reflected in the integrated CV area, which is approximately ×1.5 greater in the alkaline electrolyte than in the acidic and neutral electrolytes.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows that the surface-reconstructed catalyst behaves as a p-type semiconductor with negative Mott–Schottky slope for all interfaces. The flat band potential increases in lower pH environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was performed to understand how the (hydr)oxide/electrolyte interfaces respond to applied potential (Supplementary Fig. 10). The space charge capacitance (Cs) of semiconductor/electrolyte interfaces is related to the charge accumulation and is frequency dispersive. The Cs−2 value extracted at different frequencies decreases with potential to give a negative Mott–Schottky slope for all interfaces, indicating that the surface-reconstructed catalyst behaves as a p-type semiconductor.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando hard X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Co K edge during CV measurements tracks Co oxidation state changes. The ΔEedge increases with applied potential but changes are not fully reversible on the reverse cathodic scan. Irreversible ΔEedge increases with CV cycles in all pH environments, indicating reconstructed (hydr)oxide layers become thicker.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To study the interfacial Co oxidation state changes, we carried out operando hXAS characterizations at the Co K edge during CV measurements (Supplementary Figs. 15 and 16). The Co oxidation state change during CV measurement in an alkaline environment is tracked by the shift at the Co K edge (Fig. 4a). The Eedge of the Co K edge increases with applied potential; however, this change is not fully reversible on the reverse cathodic scan.

properties.description: Edge potential change during CV cycles

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando hXAS during chronopotentiometry shows quasi-linear relationship between ΔEedge and log(i), indicating OER current is controlled by Co oxidation state at the interface. The slope of ΔEedge versus log(i) is comparable in alkaline and acidic electrolytes but smaller in neutral electrolyte.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At a low controlled current, positive charging of the interface and oxidation of the Co sites are the dominant processes, rather than the OER. The ΔEedge (calculated by setting the Eedge at 0.01 mA as the initial state) shows a quasi-linear relationship with log(i) (Fig. 5a), indicating the OER current is controlled by the Co oxidation state at the interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy quantifies Co concentration in different electrolytes after OER. Co dissolution is less stable in acidic electrolyte with a stability number of ~59.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co concentration in the different electrolytes was quantified by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES), which is outlined in Supplementary Table 5. The stability number is calculated to be ~59 in acidic electrolyte, comparable to those of other Co-based catalysts (10^1 to 10^2 Ω) reported in the literature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface-sensitive Co L-edge spectra after OER reveal that Co species remain unchanged in alkaline electrolyte, indicating lack of obvious Co dissolution. In acidic electrolyte, CoIII species are obviously reduced after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface-sensitive Co L-edge spectra (Supplementary Figs. 30 and 31) reveal that the Co species remain unchanged after the OER in alkaline electrolyte, which is consistent with the lack of obvious Co dissolution. By comparison, the CoIII species are obviously reduced after the OER in acidic electrolyte.
